html:
The Ofayé are a small Indigenous people of central Brazil, in today's Mato Grosso do Sul, living along the Paraná River near the mouths of the Sucuriú, Ivinhema and Vacaria rivers. Their language is usually placed in the Macro-Jê family.

They hunted, gathered and farmed in the forests and savannas of the Paraná valley. Cattle ranchers took over their land in the late 1800s and 1900s, and disease and violence cut them to a few dozen people, so that they were long thought close to disappearing. Most now live on a small reserve in Brasilândia. Their neighbours included the Guató of the Pantanal to the west and the Kaingang to the south.
